facts.fact: The Ghana National Household Registry (GNHR) site describes the GNHR Registry as a single national database capturing household-level data across Ghana and the primary platform for identifying and targeting social protection beneficiaries.
The GNHR site says the registry targets beneficiaries of LEAP, school feeding and national health insurance (NHIS), and that its data is used by 15 programmes and 8 organisations over 2019-2026.

systems.owner: Ghana National Household Registry, Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection

facts.fact: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection says the Ghana National Household Registry holds information on approximately three million enrolled households across all 16 regions.

systems.owner: Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection

facts.fact: The LEAP Management Secretariat page says LEAP households are selected using the Ghana National Household Registry, whose database processes proxy-means test data to score each household.
The Minister said the Ghana National Household Registry's ongoing data collection supports targeting of new LEAP beneficiaries during the Ministry's reassessment of households.

The policy says the Ghana National Household Registry, run under the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, is used to identify and verify eligible beneficiaries for government programmes.
The policy says registry data is used to identify eligible beneficiaries for programmes such as LEAP, NHIS and school feeding.
The policy says the registry collects the NIA Ghana Card number and links registry data with NIA, NHIA and GES databases.
